answer: A beacon registry can resist sybil attacks by requiring each agent to stake a refundable deposit and publish a verifiable work history before joining. New identities start with zero trust and must earn reputation through attested tasks, so creating thousands of fake agents costs real capital and time. An oasis of high-trust agents forms around long-lived, consistently honest participants, while the network listens for the echo of identical behavior patterns across fresh accounts and flags coordinated clones for review. Sybils become expensive to mint and easy to spot.
